# PR #5208: Patch: the fork screen's save and resume tests stop playing the 96 rollout games no assertion reads

Closes #5171

The five R4607000 save/resume tests in `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` no longer play any fork arm, and together they now run in 19.97 s on this machine, against 239 s before. They keep their names and assertions, and no production code changed. One of the five mutation checks I ran was not carried through (below).

## What changed
- **New helper `trunk_only_line`:** it plays one trunk game with `play_game_probed(game, Some(Probe::scripted(game.n, answered)))`. It records the hash and fork points `play_deal` would. Each fork gets `FORK_ROLLOUTS * 2` placeholder arms, the count `load_save` checks.
- **`r4607000_resume_refuses_a_changed_header_before_any_game`:** it starts from `write_save(&path, &header, &[hand_line(1, 6, 2)])`. The twelve refusals and their checks are untouched.
- **`r4607000_a_finished_save_plays_nothing_and_reprints_its_tally`:** both runs use `echo`, so each deal is one game. It asserts the file has 2 lines, each with no forks and no arms, so it can't quietly grow again.

- **The two identity tests:** they call `trunk_only_line` instead of `play_deal`. Refusal messages and the one-call counts are unchanged.
- **`r4397000_an_always_differing_candidate_forks_every_game_at_the_cap`:** the pair check now reads `forks[1]` and asserts `fork.at_move >= 1`, so it compares a non-empty prefix.
- **`scripts/ci-shards.toml`:** the note no longer names the three tests as the binary's slowest. It says #5171 made them (and the two identity tests) play no fork arm, and that the slowest test is whatever the next measurement shows. The count stays 8.

## Tests run
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- r4607000_resume_refuses r4607000_a_finished r4607000_a_deal_finished r4607000_a_different r4607000_a_rebuilt` passed: 5 tests in **19.97 s** (35 s wall including the link).

- `r4397000_an_always_differing_candidate_forks_every_game_at_the_cap` passed at 57.9 s. The check reads move 1 and holds, so I didn't need to inspect the log.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are green. I did not run the full `fork_screen` filter, the other crates' tests or the web tests.

## Mutation checks
I removed each line by hand, ran the named test, then restored the file. `git diff` touches only the two files.

| Production line removed | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `check_header(...)` call in `resume_save` | header test | fails (0.01 s) |
| `outcome.hash != saved.hash` branch in `identity_check` | rebuilt-trunk test | fails |
| `if !same` branch in `identity_check` | different-candidate test | fails |
| finished-save early return | finished test | fails, because the factory is then called |

For the `append_deal_line` mutant, deal 2 waits for deal 1's line up to `PARTIAL_DEAL_BOUND_SECS` (1200 s) before the test fails. I stopped it rather than wait 20 minutes. By construction it fails, but only at the bound, as before this change.

# #5171: Patch: the fork screen's save and resume tests stop playing the 96 rollout games no assertion reads
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The fork screen is the tool that compares two versions of the practice AI. Five of its tests check how it saves a long run and picks it up again: a changed setting is refused, a finished save plays nothing, a half-finished batch keeps the games that already ended, and a save made by a different AI is refused. To get a save file to check, each test first plays real AI games, about 104 every time the tests run. None of the checks looks at the outcome of 96 of those games.

Once this is built, those tests write their small save files by hand (two sister tests already do), or play one quick game that never branches. They check exactly what they check today. On a 4-core machine this takes about three minutes off the slowest Rust test job, and it also speeds up the weekly mutation testing and the daily pool probe, which run the same tests. Players notice nothing. The maintainer and the bot get faster CI.

## Why

**Measured on 2026-11-27, 4 cores, the workspace's test profile (the one CI uses):**
- The `jackioh` binary's share of `rust (test tools, wasm)` (`--skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay::`, the filter in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`) ran in **587 s**. With only these five tests skipped it ran in **401 s**. So the five add 186 s, about a third of the run.
- Run alone, each takes:
  - `r4607000_resume_refuses_a_changed_header_before_any_game`: 53.6 s
  - `r4607000_a_finished_save_plays_nothing_and_reprints_its_tally`: 51.8 s
  - `r4607000_a_deal_finished_before_a_batch_error_stays_in_the_file`: 72.3 s
  - `r4607000_a_different_candidate_fails_the_identity_game`: 17.0 s
  - `r4607000_a_rebuilt_trunk_fails_the_identity_game`: 44.7 s
- The hand-written keeper `r4607000_a_hand_written_save_reprints_its_tally_without_playing` runs in under 0.1 s.

**What they play, and what they read** (`crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs`):
- `late_fork` (line 1466) forks every deal once. Each fork plays `FORK_ROLLOUTS` = 8 pairs (line 51), which is 16 arms, each nearly a whole game at `TEST_BUDGET`. So one deal is 17 games.
- `resume_refuses_a_changed_header` (line 1859) plays one live deal only to get a save. Every assertion is about `check_header`, which runs before any game (line 1007).
- `finished_save_plays_nothing` (line 2024) plays two live deals (34 games). It then makes the same three assertions the per-PR hand-written keeper (line 1579) already makes: no calls, the same tally, the file byte-identical.
- `deal_finished_before_a_batch_error` (line 1807) plays deal 1's 17 games on a two-thread pool. Deal 2's thread sleeps while it waits, so the games run one at a time. The test asserts only the number of lines and the deal number.
- The two identity tests (lines 1954 and 1989) call `play_deal` (17 games) to write the saved line, then play one identity game. `identity_check` (line 873) compares only the trunk hash and the fork points. `load_save` (line 783) checks only how many arms there are, never their results.
- That makes 104 games per run, and no assertion reads the 96 arms among them.

**The cost keeps coming back:**
- `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (lines 40-61) names these tests as the binary's slowest (90, 86 and 68 s).
- The group ran over 10 minutes three times (#4432/#4441, #4690, #4721) and now sits at 8 shards, the most allowed. The note there says the next fix would be splitting binaries or moving the slowest tests to the daily run.
- The maintainers already took the cheap route twice in this file. #4690 replaced two live r4607000 tests with hand-written keepers (lines 1574-1632 and 1695-1745). #4462 moved a 16-arm test to the daily run (line 1325).
- Others pay for the same tests:
  - `scripts/mutants.sh` (lines 52-58) caps a tools shard at 30 mutants because this binary's tests take about 7.5 of the suite's 8 minutes for every mutant.
  - `super.yml` (lines 307-311): the pool probe's tools leg ran past 60 minutes on 2026-11-26.
  - `PARTIAL_DEAL_BOUND_SECS` = 1200 (line 1804) exists because one of these deals "takes minutes on a small runner, and longer under the pool probe".

**A check in the same module that cannot fail:** `r4397000_an_always_differing_candidate_forks_every_game_at_the_cap` checks the arms' shared prefix on `forks[0]` (lines 1307-1315). That fork's `at_move` is 0 (asserted at line 1295), so the check compares two empty slices. This is the per-PR test that the daily-moved thread test (line 1325) names as keeping pair determinism.

## Proposal

This changes tests only, in `fork_screen.rs`'s `mod tests`; no production code changes. Each test keeps its name, its rule and its assertions.

1. **`resume_refuses_a_changed_header_before_any_game`:** start from `write_save(&path, &test_header(1), &[hand_line(1, 6, 2)])` instead of a live deal. Keep the same twelve header changes and the same checks: the refusal names the field, nothing is played, the file is left unchanged, and the file ends as it was written.
2. **`finished_save_plays_nothing_and_reprints_its_tally`:** play its live run with the existing `echo` candidate, which never forks, so each deal is one game. The path from the live writer to the reader to a finished save stays tested per PR, for 2 games. Assert that each saved line has no forks, so the test cannot quietly grow again.
3. **`deal_finished_before_a_batch_error_stays_in_the_file`:** deal 1 uses `echo` (one game). Deal 2 still waits for deal 1's line and then fails. Same assertions.
4. **The two identity tests:** a test helper builds the saved line from the trunk alone. It calls `play_game_probed(&game, Some(Probe::scripted(1, late_fork)))` and records the hash and fork points `play_deal` would record, with `FORK_ROLLOUTS * 2` placeholder arms per fork (what `load_save` checks). Each test then plays 2 trunk games instead of 18, with the same refusal messages and call counts.
5. **The prefix check:** make it read the second fork (`at_move` 1), so it compares a prefix that is not empty.
6. **`scripts/ci-shards.toml`:** update the note that names these tests as the slowest.

The live writer with arms stays tested by the two daily tests #4690 kept for it (`r4607000_resume_after_cut_prints_the_same_tally` and `r4607000_a_torn_last_line_is_played_again`), as their ignore reasons already say. `FORK_ROLLOUTS`, production code and the daily tests stay as they are.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs`, tests module only.
- `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, the comment on the `tools, wasm` count.
- No spec change. R4607000 and R4397000 keep their proving tests, whose names stay, so `spec check` is unaffected. SPEC §9.9 (the fork screen) does not change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The five r4607000 tests keep their names and pass. None is ignored, emptied or deleted.
- [ ] Each keeps today's assertions:
  - the twelve header refusals, each naming its field, with no game played and the file unchanged;
  - a finished save: no calls, the same tally and duel lines, the file byte-identical;
  - a failed batch keeps exactly deal 1's line;
  - the identity refusals name `forks` and `trunk hash`, after exactly one call each.
- [ ] None of the five plays a fork's arm: no `play_deal`, and no live `resume_save` with a forking candidate. The `echo` deals assert that they have no forks.
- [ ] Each test still fails when the production line it guards is removed by hand:
  - the `check_header` call in `resume_save`;
  - the per-deal `append_deal_line`;
  - the hash comparison and the fork comparison in `identity_check`;
  - the finished-save early return.
- [ ] The pair test's prefix check compares a non-empty prefix (`fork.at_move >= 1`).
- [ ] The five together finish in under 20 s on a 4-core machine (239 s today), and the PR reports what it measured.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh fork_screen`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are green.
- [ ] `scripts/ci-shards.toml` no longer names these tests as the binary's slowest.

## Size and risks

- **Size:** small and medium difficulty. One test module, roughly 60 to 100 lines changed, no production code.
- **Risk: per-PR coverage of `play_deal` packing arms into a saved line goes away.** The two daily tests named above keep that rule. Per PR, the hand-written keeper still covers reading arms back, and the cap test still plays a pair.
- **Risk: the `echo` deal might fork after all.** Then the test would be slow again without anyone noticing, which the no-forks assertion catches.
- **Measurement caveat:** each timing is one run on one 4-core machine, not CI's runner. CI's per-shard saving depends on which of the 8 hash shards each test lands in.
